text:
Nina Gomez: FYI ran into duplicated webhook deliveries in the python sampleapp while testing 429 surge behavior. single click resulted in two downstream POSTs.

Arjun Rao: rough. which SDK + sampleapp version?

Nina Gomez: python-sdk 1.6.0 + sampleapp v0.10.0 local. I have a tiny repro script that flips token creds mid-backoff and disables client jitter (we toggle jitter=false in test env). logs: 
```
2026-03-22T20:12:01.345Z INFO req=xyz status=429
2026-03-22T20:12:01.346Z INFO backoff=100ms jitter=0 req=xyz
2026-03-22T20:12:01.350Z WARN token rotated while in_backoff
2026-03-22T20:12:01.451Z INFO req=xyz status=200 side_effect=applied
2026-03-22T20:12:01.452Z INFO req=xyz_retry status=200 side_effect=applied (duplicate)
```

Priya Singh: that pattern screams unsafe-replay + missing resume guard. do our python sdk and go sdk behave the same if jitter is off?

Nina Gomez: i tested go quickly — it preserved the idempotency header across resume. python didn't. i suspect a small code path where the retry wrapper rebuilds headers after token refresh and drops the Idempotency-Key.

Arjun Rao: parity gap then. two actionable fixes: (A) ensure all SDKs persist Idempotency-Key across token rotation and resume logic; (B) make client jitter enabled by default for 429/backoff to reduce synchronized retries.

Priya Singh: agree. also add a server-side short dedupe window (configurable) to guard apps that misconfigure clients. propose default 8s safe_replay_window. that balances observed ~1-3s races + network lag.

Nina Gomez: +1. for onboarding docs we should call out "if you rotate credentials or refresh tokens during requests, store idempotency keys in a place that survives refresh events (e.g., request-scoped cache)."

DevX Bot: created issue DEVEX-1122 "python SDK: preserve Idempotency-Key across resume paths" and assigned to @Priya. PR template added.

Priya Singh: i'll take DEVEX-1122. plan: (1) add unit test that simulates token refresh callback and asserts header survives, (2) add end-to-end sampleapp chaos test `tests/chaos/test_token_rotate_429.py`, (3) flip python default jitter to true in 1.6.1 with opt-out.

Arjun Rao: for SDK parity matrix, i'll run cross-SDK harness and dump results to S3. also will add a short-lived feature flag in sampleapp to toggle `safe_replay_window_ms`.

Nina Gomez: i pushed repro branch `devex/python-replay-guard` and a minimal run script: `./scripts/repro_token_rotate_429.sh`. it spins up local auth server and flips creds after initial 429.

ops-bot: CI queued: devex/sampleapp#chaos (test_token_rotate_429)

Arjun Rao: telemetry note: emit metric `sdk.replayed_request.count` with tags sdk:python|go|node and reason:token_rotate|server_429. we can alert if duplicates > X/day.

Priya Singh: implemented header preservation in local branch, writing tests now. small question: should we also preserve any custom user-provided headers (e.g., X-Correlation-Id) or only Idempotency-Key?

Nina Gomez: i'd preserve Idempotency-Key and X-Correlation-Id. correlation helps tracing when dedupe window hits. but make it explicit in SDK docs which headers are retained on resume.

Arjun Rao: one more thing: add a linchpin in quickstart: `Best practice: always set Idempotency-Key for non-idempotent operations. SDKs will preserve it across token refresh by default.`

DevX Bot: linked DEVEX-1122 to docs task DEVEX-1123 and CI task DEVEX-1124

Priya Singh: will open PRs today, request reviews from @Arjun and @Nina. will also add changelog entry for python 1.6.1.

Nina Gomez: thanks all. once PRs merged can we add the chaos test to nightly CI and roll a micro-release? i'd like to close the repro branch after verifying.

Arjun Rao: yep. after python change we should run the cross-sdk harness to confirm behavior parity. leaving a TODO to evaluate default safe_replay_window_ms value from production telemetry after 2 weeks. :spiral_calendar:
